title: 📰 AI news · November 13

items.title: 4,800 GitHub accounts hijacked to steal keys
items.text: Attackers took over 4,837 GitHub accounts and probed 61,764 repositories. They planted a script that grabs cloud and AI-service keys: AWS, Azure, OpenAI, Anthropic. If you run a bot or an agent on AI, its keys may sit in your repository settings. Check today which keys your repository can see. Free guide “Protect your computer, code and access” — send the word “защита” to the bot.

items.title: Apify replaced API keys for 80,000 customers
items.text: An outsider got into Apify's internal systems on November 9 and 10. The company replaced customer API keys and proxy passwords and closed all sessions. If you run scrapers or agents through Apify, your keys are already new, but you need to set up two-factor protection again. Open the console and do it today.

items.title: Police took down 235 servers used by malware
items.text: Europol and police from nine countries seized 235 servers and 257 domains used by Gootloader, StealC and CastleRAT. These programs loaded other malware, stole passwords and wallets, and gave attackers remote access to computers.

items.title: Google released Gemini 4 Hydrogen
items.text: The new model replaces the Flash line and nearly matches Claude Sonnet 5.5 on the Artificial Analysis index. A million tokens cost $1.50 in and $7.50 out. It is available in the Gemini API, Antigravity and the Gemini app.

items.title: ElevenLabs released Scribe v3 speech recognition
items.text: The model knows 102 languages and makes about 25 percent fewer errors than the previous version. The Live version is built for voice agents and does not cut people off mid-sentence. A thousand minutes cost $3.33.

items.title: Jensen Huang stepped down as Nvidia CEO
items.text: He left his posts as CEO, president and board member, and the company lost about $1.4 trillion in value. CFO Colette Kress will lead it on an interim basis.

items.title: US moves to seize over $1.2B stolen from Binance
items.text: A court authorized seizing more than $1.2 billion; more than $2.7 billion is frozen out of over $6 billion stolen. The FBI also seized servers of the FaceStealer scheme, where North Korean hackers lure people into fake video calls and infect their computers. If someone unexpectedly invites you to a call and asks you to download something, check who it is first.

items.title: Spy boards found in three Trezor Safe 5 wallets
items.text: The wallets were bought from reseller CryptoBilis between August 20 and September 23. An extra board copies the screen, stores recovery phrases and sends them over the mobile network. Firmware 2.13.1 from November 11 blocks such boards; no customer has reported losing funds.

items.title: Anthropic's scanner found a critical Apache flaw
items.text: A flaw in the HTTP/2 module of versions 2.4.55–2.4.70 lets attackers run code on the server. The fix shipped in 2.4.71 on November 11. If your site runs on Apache, ask your developer to check the version.

items.title: Salesforce opened SOV-Transcribe-1 speech recognition
items.text: A 26-billion-parameter model with 4 billion active, under Apache 2.0. Its error rate is 2.28 percent, first among open models on Artificial Analysis. You can run it yourself without sending audio out.

items.title: Google's Gemini glasses open for pre-order
items.text: Made by Warby Parker and Gentle Monster with Samsung. About 41 grams, up to 9 hours of use, speech translation from more than 70 languages. From $395, on sale December 10 in the US and South Korea.

takeaway: Today's news is about keys: they are stolen from repositories, and platforms replace them after breaches. Recommendation: open the settings of your repositories and services, remove unused keys and turn two-factor protection on again.
cta: 🔐 Check where my keys are stored
